title: A Little Jazz Vocabulary
description: Explore jazz through familiar instruments, group names, and the words describing rhythm and spontaneous playing.
cardDescription: Explore jazz through familiar instruments, group names, and the words describing rhythm and spontaneous playing.
focus: The clues describe musical sounds and performance roles. No recording dates or named soloists are needed.
solvingTip: Look for an instrument, a group, or something a musician does during a performance.
words: Music style associated with improvisation and rhythmic variety
Rhythmic feel also naming a familiar jazz era and style
Passage played by one featured musician
Instrument family including trumpet and trombone
Percussion instrument supporting a jazz rhythm
Keyboard instrument often heard in a jazz trio
Short musical phrase repeated during a performance
To create musical ideas while performing
Pattern of musical timing and accents

answerNotes.RIFF: A riff is a short recurring phrase. It names a musical idea rather than a whole song.
answerNotes.COMBO: Combo is short for combination. In jazz it commonly names a small performing group.
answerNotes.IMPROVISE: Improvisation creates musical ideas during performance. It differs from following every note of a fully written part.
answerNotes.SOLO: A solo features one performer. Other players may still provide accompaniment beneath that featured part.

title: Country Music on the Radio
description: Meet familiar country-music sounds through instruments, song forms, and everyday performance words.
cardDescription: Meet familiar country-music sounds through instruments, song forms, and everyday performance words.
focus: The clues describe instruments and ways songs are presented. Their jobs and shapes identify them without artist-name trivia.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for an instrument, a voice feature, or a song section.
words: American music style associated with storytelling songs and string instruments
Six-string instrument commonly strummed in a country band
Informal name for a violin in country and folk music
String instrument with a round drumlike body
Word before guitar for an instrument often played with a sliding bar
Distinctive ringing or nasal musical sound
Song section whose words change as the story continues
Song section commonly returning with the same words
Footwear associated with a country-dance outfit
Raised area where a country band performs

answerNotes.FIDDLE: Fiddle and violin can name the same instrument. The music setting and playing tradition influence which word is used.
answerNotes.BANJO: A banjo has strings over a round drumlike body. That construction distinguishes it from a typical guitar.
answerNotes.BALLAD: A ballad tells a story in song. It is a song form rather than the name of one performer.
answerNotes.TWANG: Twang describes a characteristic sound. The word does not identify a fixed pitch or one instrument alone.

title: Words from a Blues Session
description: Follow a blues session through familiar instrument names, repeating phrases, and performance actions.
cardDescription: Follow a blues session through familiar instrument names, repeating phrases, and performance actions.
focus: The clues describe the vocabulary of a musical gathering. Some answers name equipment, while others name a sound or a way musicians respond.
solvingTip: Use the instrument and group clues to cross the words describing musical expression.
words: Music tradition associated with expressive singing and recurring musical patterns
Informal name for a harmonica in blues music
String instrument often used for blues melodies and accompaniment
Smooth object moved along guitar strings to change pitch
To alter a musical note’s pitch expressively
Recurring short phrase in a blues performance
Section carrying a set of lyrics in a blues song
Short name for an electronic sound amplifier
Featured passage for one blues performer
Opening musical phrase inviting a response
Musical phrase answering an earlier call

answerNotes.HARP: Harp can mean harmonica in blues vocabulary. The clue does not ask for the large triangular string instrument.
answerNotes.SLIDE: A guitar slide moves along the strings. It helps change pitch smoothly rather than selecting only one fixed fret.
answerNotes.AMP: Amp is short for amplifier. It names equipment used to increase an electrical audio signal.
answerNotes.RESPONSE: Call and response pairs one musical phrase with an answer. The terms describe how parts relate to each other.

title: A Folk Song Gathering
description: Gather familiar folk-music words for instruments, storytelling, and singing together.
cardDescription: Gather familiar folk-music words for instruments, storytelling, and singing together.
focus: The clues focus on shared music-making. A song, a repeated section, and a musical group have distinct names.
solvingTip: Look for an instrument, a song form, or something shared by the singers.
words: Music associated with shared traditions and community songs
Describing an instrument that produces its normal sound without electronic amplification
Round-bodied string instrument heard in many folk ensembles
Violin used in a folk-playing setting
Small string instrument commonly having four pairs of strings
Plucked or strummed string instrument supporting a folk song
Narrative song passed along in a singing tradition
Repeated words or musical section returning in a song
Melody carried by a traditional song
One worded part of a song, commonly used in the plural
Group of singers joining a shared song
Arrangement of people gathered around a music-making space
Account of events told through a folk song
To make musical sounds with the voice

answerNotes.MANDOLIN: A common mandolin has paired strings called courses. The small body and paired strings distinguish it from a standard guitar.
answerNotes.REFRAIN: A refrain returns within a song. The repeated section can help listeners join in.
answerNotes.ACOUSTIC: An acoustic instrument produces its normal sound without needing an electronic amplifier. A microphone or pickup can still be used to record or amplify it.
answerNotes.BALLAD: A ballad is a narrative song here. The clue uses the storytelling form rather than a particular title.

title: Rock and Roll Sounds
description: Explore a familiar amplified band through instruments, equipment, and the words for a strong musical pulse.
cardDescription: Explore a familiar amplified band through instruments, equipment, and the words for a strong musical pulse.
focus: The clues use everyday band vocabulary. They ask what an object or musical feature is, not who released a song.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue describes equipment, a playing role, or a repeating musical idea.
words: Music style associated with amplified guitars and a strong beat

Returning song section often joined by an audience
Performance area occupied by a live band
To move the body in response to music
Additional performance requested after a concert ends

answerNotes.MIC: Mic is a common abbreviation for microphone. The spelling is short even though it is pronounced like mike.
answerNotes.BASS: Bass names the low musical register and rhymes with base. The fish name uses another pronunciation.
answerNotes.ENCORE: An encore is an additional performance after the planned ending. The word can also be the audience’s request for more.
answerNotes.CABLE: A cable carries an electrical signal between equipment. It is separate from the acoustic sound traveling through the room.
